title: Grade matrix and coach rows with the live entity index, like the rail
body:
## Summary
deriveEntityArtifacts gets the live entity index from the rail (useBaseline) but an empty {} from the Matrix and the global coach, so link-aware checkers see has()=false there.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/matrixRows.ts:58 and src/components/layout-lab/globalCoachModel.ts:124 call deriveEntityArtifacts(..., {}, verdicts). buildLabCheckerContext (src/components/layout-lab/labCheckerContext.ts:59) turns that into has: (c, e) => !!{}[c]?.[e], i.e. "no entity anywhere exists" - the exact pessimistic default the labCheckerContext doc (lines 22-27) says it removed. The rail passes the catalog store's index (src/components/layout-lab/Baseline/useBaseline.ts:144). For a step with server truth the overlay adopts the server verdict over a local deferred, so the gap shows on locally produced content with no (or an older) server row: rail pass, Matrix cell + coach candidate deferred. Fixed = CoachCatalogInput / buildMatrixRows take the entity index and pass it through (useGlobalCoach already reads the store).

## Flow
- produce a linksResolve step locally whose link target exists, before the write-through lands
- rail dot: pass; Matrix cell and Do-next row: deferred
- fix: thread entitiesByCatalog into buildCatalogCandidates/buildCatalogCandidatesFromSummary and matrixRows

## Expected impact
Matrix, coach and rail agree on link-aware steps (65+ per the labCheckerContext doc). Could break: the coach per-catalog memo must key on the index reference.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one CheckerContext truth across rail, matrix, coach
Before: 2 of 3 deriveEntityArtifacts call sites pass {} (grep)
After: predicted 0 of 3
Method: simulation - walked the local-only produce case; seam is in catalog-pipeline-state files outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/layout-lab/matrixRows.ts:58 deriveEntityArtifacts(catalogId, e, own, effective, serverArts, {}, verdicts)
src/components/layout-lab/globalCoachModel.ts:124 deriveEntityArtifacts(cin.catalogId, e, own, effective, serverArts, {}, verdicts)
src/components/layout-lab/Baseline/useBaseline.ts:144 useEntityArtifacts(..., serverArts, entitiesByCatalog)
instrument: a deriveEntityArtifacts test: a linksResolve step with local content, no server row, target entity seeded -> rail-path pass vs matrixRows/buildCatalogCandidates deferred; red before, green after

title: Scope the global coach summary fan-out to the active game's catalogs
body:
## Summary
useGlobalCoach fetches a summary for every registered catalog and holds loading until all settle, including catalogs the active game does not show.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/hooks/useGlobalCoach.ts: catalogIds = CATALOG_SECTIONS (all 37); the effect calls ensureSummary for each, and loading counts every section. Under gtai scope.visible is 30 of 37 (scopeCatalogIds probe), so 7 summary GETs per first paint are never used and a slow out-of-scope catalog keeps the Do-next row on its loading state. Fixed = fetch and count loading over scope.visible only (the comment's "unhydrated store reads as loading" holds over the visible list).

## Flow
- switch to gtai, open the lab
- 37 /api/pipeline-artifacts/summary GETs fire; 30 contribute
- fix: iterate scope.visible in the effect and the loading predicate

## Expected impact
GTAI first paint issues 30 summary reads instead of 37, and loading settles on the catalogs actually coached. PoF unchanged (visible = all). Could break: a game switch must re-run the effect (scope is already a dep).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer first-paint reads under a scoped game
Before: 37 summary fetches under gtai (CATALOG_SECTIONS length; scope.visible = 30, measured by probe)
After: predicted 30
Method: probe - scopeCatalogIds('gtai', 37 ids) = 30 visible; fetch count not re-run on a patched hook
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: renderHook(useGlobalCoach) under gtai counting fetchStepSummaryResult calls (37 -> 30), plus the derivation cost suite unchanged

title: Let useRovingFocus own the sync to the externally selected index
body:
## Summary
Both useRovingFocus consumers hand-roll the same render-phase "resync active to the selected index" bail-out.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/CatalogTree.tsx:353-358 and src/components/layout-lab/PipelineRail.tsx:105-110 each keep a prev-value state and call roving.setActive when the selected index changes. The hook takes initial but ignores later values, so every consumer must repeat the bail-out or its cursor drifts from the selection. Fixed = the hook adopts a changed initial (renamed selected) itself with the same render-phase pattern; both copies are deleted.

## Flow
- hook: track prev selected, setActive on change
- delete the two consumer copies
- run CatalogTree.keyboard + PipelineRail suites

## Expected impact
One owner for the rule; a third consumer cannot forget it. Could break: a consumer that wanted the cursor NOT to follow selection (none today).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of the cursor-follows-selection rule
Before: 2 hand-rolled copies (grep prevActiveIdx / prevWant)
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - consumers are in catalog-browser-ui / lab-shell files outside this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/layout-lab/CatalogTree.tsx:355 const [prevActiveIdx, setPrevActiveIdx] = useState(activeIdx);
src/components/layout-lab/PipelineRail.tsx:107 const [prevWant, setPrevWant] = useState(want);
instrument: a useRovingFocus test that changes the initial/selected prop and asserts the tab-stop follows, plus CatalogTree.keyboard and PipelineRail suites green with both copies deleted
